title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Theater on 1969-04-26
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > USB > WaveLab Mastering: In WaveLab with Nomad Factory Plugins > CD Wave > TLH > Flac
source: Soundboard Cassette x 1 > DAT; Encore Source: 7 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk > DAT

ai_review.summary: Solid 1969 soundboard captures a fiery early‑Dead show with smoking Viola jam, Minglewood Blues and Silver Threads shining.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced 1969 soundboard tape – not perfect but surprisingly clear for its era, despite occasional quiet spots and a low mix on Pig. Musically the concert is a highlight of the spring‑'69 era, featuring standout performances of Minglewood Blues, Silver Threads, Dupree's Diamond Blues and an incendiary Viola > Caution Jam > Viola sequence that reviewers call “smoking”. Overall the show is praised for its primal emotion and tight band interplay.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (mostly 5★) and enthusiastic comments about both the performance and the soundboard quality lead to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Solid 1969 board recording, generally clear with front‑center Jerry and Phil; some sections are quieter than others and Pig (Ron) is low in the mix, but overall very listenable.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Eleven Jam > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, early‑spring set that builds momentum through a strong first half and erupts in the second set with extended jams; the Viola jam is highlighted as the climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Prominent front‑and‑center with a smoking lead on the Viola section; his tone praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Right up front, delivering powerful bass that drives the jams, especially during the extended second‑set sequences.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides vocal work and engages in memorable banter with Pig after "Doin' That Rag" about drum monitors.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig (Ron) is noted as being low in the mix; no specific praise of keyboard performance beyond that.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann is highlighted as solid and forward‑placed in the mix, keeping a strong rhythmic foundation.
